question: Sapna invested ₹22,400 on simple interest, partly at 13% per annum and partly at 3% per annum. If she earns equal interests from the two investments after 7 years, then find the sum invested at 13% per annum (in ₹).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For equal simple interests over the same time, the ratio of Principals is the inverse of the ratio of Rates.

P₁ : P₂ = R₂ : R₁ = 3 : 13

Total parts = 3 + 13 = 16 parts ≡ ₹22,400 ⇒ 1 part = ₹1,400

Sum invested at 13% (P₁) = 3 × 1400 = ₹4,200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Investment = ₹22,400

Rate for Part 1 (R₁) = 13% per annum

Rate for Part 2 (R₂) = 3% per annum

Time (T) = 7 years for both

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
 Total: ₹22,400
 
• 
 
• 
 
 Part 1 (P1)
 13% for 7 years
 
 Part 2 (P2)
 3% for 7 years
 
• 
 
• 
 
 Simple Interest 1 = Simple Interest 2

**Calculation:**

Let the sum invested at 13% be P₁ and at 3% be P₂.

⇒ P₁ + P₂ = 22400

Given that the interests from both investments are equal after 7 years:

⇒ (P₁ × 13 × 7) ÷ 100 = (P₂ × 3 × 7) ÷ 100

⇒ P₁ × 13 = P₂ × 3

⇒ P₁ ÷ P₂ = 3 ÷ 13

The total ratio parts = 3 + 13 = 16 parts

⇒ 16 parts = 22400

⇒ 1 part = 22400 ÷ 16 = 1400

The sum invested at 13% corresponds to 3 parts:

⇒ P₁ = 3 × 1400 = 4200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

When Final Amounts are Equal

If the total amounts (Principal + SI) from two parts are equal, the ratio of their principals is P₁ : P₂ = (100 + R₂T₂) : (100 + R₁T₁).

Simple Interest Rule

Simple Interest is calculated only on the initial principal amount. SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Difference Between SI and CI (2 Years)

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for 2 years is calculated as D = P(R ÷ 100)².
